refusedToInherit: B6's counts (78,428 situsCity / 17,674 situsZip / 103,913 acreage). The dispatch instructs re-derivation and B6's own close records that it left a conclusion standing on a corrected instrument. Every number in this lane comes from a scan run in this session.
B6's framing that the sibling population IS the absence population. That framing is INCOMPLETE and the incompleteness is this lane's first finding.

theGapInB6sOwnSiblingCount.claim: B6 measured the siblings as leaf-cells currently served as an earned absence object whose declared-vintage cad_property row carries a usable value. That is the ABSENCE-to-VALUE direction only.
theGapInB6sOwnSiblingCount.whatItMisses: Roll-over-claim precedence ALSO changes every cell where BOTH sources carry a value and they DISAGREE. For situsAddress B6 built provenance.situsAddressSupersededClaim for exactly that case and never counted its population. For situsCity that population is the whole question: a parcel whose claim says one city and whose declared roll says another is a parcel whose zoning-jurisdiction fallback may already be moving.
theGapInB6sOwnSiblingCount.whyItMattersMoreForCityThanForAddress: situsAddress is display. situsCity is an INPUT to resolveZoningJurisdiction. An address that changes is a corrected label; a city that changes is potentially a different jurisdiction, a different zoning layer, and a different provenance URL.
theGapInB6sOwnSiblingCount.consequenceForThisLane: the census run here measures FIVE populations per leaf, not one: absence-with-recoverable-roll, value-agree, value-disagree, claim-only-roll-blank, and genuinely-absent-both.

codeReadFindings_beforeAnyMeasurement.note: ENFORCEMENT: code reading outranks output measuring. These are read at source in this worktree, with file and line, before the scan returned.

f1_situsCityReachesZoningOnlyAsAFallback.rule: a non-empty zoningJurisdiction stamp WINS UNCONDITIONALLY (line 574-575: a stamped-but-unknown key still returns before situs is read). situsCity is consulted ONLY when the stamp is empty AND countyFips is set AND wiredZoningCityKeys(fips) is non-empty AND the normalised situs contains a wired layer's normalised cityName.
f1_situsCityReachesZoningOnlyAsAFallback.consequence: the movable population is NOT 78k. It is bounded by (stamp empty) AND (situsCity changes across the wired-name predicate). Both bounds must be measured, not assumed.

f2_theBakedJurisdictionOnlyExistsWhereAD.rule: zoning is null unless zoningDistrict (row.zoning_district) is a non-empty string. jurisdictionKey and the layer provenance are computed but only SURVIVE onto the payload inside that branch.
f2_theBakedJurisdictionOnlyExistsWhereAD.consequence: a situsCity change on a parcel with no baked district changes zoning not at all. It changes envelope.jurisdictionKey, and the envelope is stripped at serve (brokerageNodeFacets.ts:621 stripZombieEnvelopeFromFacets).

f3_theSERVEOverridesTheBakedZoningEntire.rule: when parcelRecordZoningFact has genuinely earned a state (present, absent-verified, not-applicable, or code parcel-record-engine-refused) it REPLACES out.zoning wholesale -- district, jurisdictionKey and provenance all come from the Factory parcel_record rail, never from the bake. The baked stamp only survives where the rail has NOT earned a state.
f3_theSERVEOverridesTheBakedZoningEntire.consequence: this is the single most important fact for the zoning question and it is not in the dispatch. The baked jurisdictionKey a situsCity change would move is, for every slated county-rail pair, already overridden before a customer sees it. The population that can actually serve a WRONG jurisdiction because of situsCity is bounded by the parcels where the rail has earned nothing.

f4_situsZipHasExactlyOneConsumerAndItIsD.where: grep of src/ excluding tests: the only reader of baseFacts.situsZip outside the bake/assembler is lib/smartSiteStub.ts:179, which passes it as one of four parts to composeSitusLabel.
f4_situsZipHasExactlyOneConsumerAndItIsD.consequence: situsZip is display-only. No routing, no gate, no join key, no jurisdiction.

f5_computeTier1EnvelopeTakesSitusCityAnd.rule: the function's Tier1EnvelopeInput carries situsCity and the body references only zoningCode and zoningJurisdictionFallback. The comment at nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts:1155 names computeTier1Envelope as a situsCity consumer; at source it is not one.
f5_computeTier1EnvelopeTakesSitusCityAnd.consequence: a documented consumer that does not consume. Recorded rather than fixed -- it is a dead parameter, not a defect that serves anything wrong.

f6_cad_propertyCarriesAllThreeColumns.finding: cad_property has situs_city, situs_zip AND land_acres (numeric). fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll (lib/joinIntegrityGate.ts:387-395) selects none of them. Same shape B6 found for situs_address: the ROW is already in hand, the COLUMNS are not in the SELECT.
f6_cad_propertyCarriesAllThreeColumns.consequence: all three leaves are recoverable with no new query, exactly as the dispatch says.

f7_namingInconsistencyFlagged.finding: two ZONING_LAYERS record keys, elgin-tx (countyFips 48021) and elgin-tx-travis (countyFips 48453), both carry cityKey elgin-tx. wiredZoningCityKeys maps over the VALUES cityKey, so 48453's wired set contains elgin-tx; resolveZoningJurisdiction then looks up ZONING_LAYERS[elgin-tx] by RECORD KEY and gets the BASTROP entry. The cityName matches either way so today it resolves to the same string, but a record key and its own cityKey field disagreeing is a latent trap for any future lookup that assumes they are the same.
f7_namingInconsistencyFlagged.disposition: flagged, not fixed. Out of this card's scope (cad-ingest zoning registry, not the tier-1 bake). Recommend making the lookup key-by-value or renaming so record key equals cityKey.

instrumentDefectFoundInTheInheritedInstr.text: situsCity: declaredRow?.situs_city ?? null,  and  situsZip: declaredRow?.situs_zip ?? null,
instrumentDefectFoundInTheInheritedInstr.defect: the instrument synthesises the CLAIM's situsCity and situsZip FROM THE DECLARED ROLL. For B6's purpose (situsAddress) that was harmless: those two fields were never the leaf under test. For THIS lane it is fatal -- it would make claim and roll agree by construction on precisely the two leaves being decided, and every before/after would show no movement. Reusing it unmodified would have produced a confidently wrong nothing-moves result.
instrumentDefectFoundInTheInheritedInstr.fix: the extension reads the claim's situsCity/situsZip out of the STORED payload the way B6 recovered the claim's raw situsAddress (string leaf = the claim value verbatim; absence object = the claim carried nothing), never from cad_property.
instrumentDefectFoundInTheInheritedInstr.whyThisIsFiledHere: this is the same class as B6's own I2 (reading a proxy for the authoritative record). It was found by reading the instrument before running it, which is the only way it could have been found -- the wrong version would have PASSED.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.note: DEV_PROCESS 4.5 and ENFORCEMENT pre-register the falsifier for your own checks. Stated BEFORE the scan returned.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.p1: situsCity recoverable (absence to roll value) reproduces B6's 78,428 within a small residue. If it differs by more than ~1%, B6's counting rule and mine differ and the difference is the finding, not a rounding.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.p2: situsCity DISAGREE (both present, different) is NON-ZERO and I expect it to be LARGER than the recoverable population on Travis, because Travis's claim is a 2025 StratMap drop and its declared roll is a 2026 PACS export. If DISAGREE is zero, my whole one-payload-two-vintages premise is wrong for this leaf and I must say so.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.p3: acreage refused-with-recoverable-land_acres is non-zero on Bastrop specifically, because the dispatch names a 2026-09-10 re-bake that wrote 15,542 Bastrop rows refused. If it is zero, either the re-bake did not land or land_acres is empty in the 2025 Bastrop roll -- either way a finding.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.p4: the number of parcels whose zoning JURISDICTION actually moves is FAR smaller than the number of situsCity cells that change, because of code-read findings f1/f2/f3. If it is of the same order, one of those three reads is wrong and I must re-read it.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.whatWouldProveTheWholeCardWrong: if the declared roll's situs_city were systematically emptier or worse than the claim's, roll-over-claim precedence would be a REGRESSION for this leaf and B6's precedence would not generalise. city_claim_only_rollblank is the column that would show it.

plannedDisposition_provisional.situsZip: IMPLEMENT roll-over-claim. Display-only consumer, no routing, symmetrical with situsAddress. Lowest risk of the three.
plannedDisposition_provisional.acreage: MEASURE FIRST, then decide. The specific finding the dispatch wants is refused-over-recoverable, which is an ENFORCEMENT inversion (serving a declared refusal over data held). If the count is material, implement a declared-roll land_acres source ABOVE the claim fallback and BELOW the ring, and give it its own method string so it is not silently mixed with cad-roll-land-acres from the claim.
plannedDisposition_provisional.situsCity: DECIDE AT THE BOUNDARY. If the measured jurisdiction movement is a correction with evidence, implement. If it needs a policy call about which vintage owns jurisdiction assignment, stop and report. The dispatch explicitly authorises stopping and this checkpoint records that stopping is not a failure mode here.
